architecture.approach: One data path, four presentations. client/src/pages/TaskPage.tsx owns the state (useTasks for data, the URL for the view, filters and board controls) and passes tasks plus callbacks into the selected view, which implements TaskViewProps (views/types.ts). Every view keeps its non-visual rules in client/src/features/tasks/lib/ with unit tests, and everything a user can be looking at (view, filters, board column, quick filters, grouping) is parsed from and written to the query string by small pure helpers. Drag and drop uses platform primitives - native HTML5 DnD for the board and the calendar, pointer events for the Gantt - and each gesture has a keyboard or button equivalent.

dataModel.flowDescription: TaskPage loads the workspace's tasks through useTasks (one shared cached list), applies the URL-held filters in memory and renders the requested view with the filtered tasks plus the write/delete capabilities. A view never fetches: it calls back into the page's handlers (onUpdate, onCreate, onDelete, onOpen), and those go through useTasks, which patches optimistically and rolls back on failure. Board and calendar drops send a small PATCH (position, stage/status, deadline, startDate); the Gantt sends shiftTask/resizeTask patches. Board controls (column, quick filters, grouping) and the view and filters all live in the query string, so a view is reproducible from its link.

securityConsiderations.description: canWrite and canDelete only hide or disable affordances (inline editors, drag, quick move, delete); the API keeps enforcing tasks:write and tasks:delete through requirePermission, so hiding a control is never the security boundary (EC-009).

Everything a gesture can do has a keyboard path (column tabs, Gantt arrow keys, the Move-to sheet, the done button), which also keeps the views usable without a pointer; accessible names come from the design-system primitives and explicit labels.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: All four views render the one cached task list from useTasks, so switching view or returning to the page costs no extra request, and an update patches that list in place instead of refetching it.
Phones render a single board column with week-zoom Gantt and cards instead of the table, and every board column paginates at ten cards, keeping the DOM small on the devices with the least headroom.
Reordering writes one fractional position instead of renumbering the column, so a drop is a single small PATCH, and the board keeps the dragged card's state locally until that patch resolves.

risks.description: Keyboard and touch alternatives can be forgotten when a gesture is added, leaving one device class unable to act.
risks.mitigation: The board's phone path, the Gantt's arrow keys and the list's selection keys have their own tests (board.test.tsx, calendar.test.tsx, views.test.tsx), and any drag handler is written next to its non-drag equivalent.

risks.description: The URL can grow stale or contradictory while a user clicks around (unknown stage, removed label filter).
risks.mitigation: Every parsed value falls back to a default, `?col=` returns to the first stage by dropping the parameter, and filter targets that no longer exist fall back to "all".

risks.description: Live refreshes during an interaction (drag, resize, long press) can move the data under the user.
risks.mitigation: useLiveHold pauses refreshes while a Gantt drag is active and the board keeps its own drop state until the patch resolves.
